name: Website Helpers and Resource Directories
title: Website Helpers and Resource Directories
answer: A website helper is a chat tool on a district website that answers common family questions about enrollment, schedules, and services at any hour, using only verified district information and saying clearly when it does not know. A family resource directory helps families find services such as food assistance, health care, and tutoring, and a chat tool limited to a verified list can help them search it. This matters because families need reliable access to help, but the helper must never be the only route, so a staffed phone line and email stay available and easy to find.

sections.body: Many families have questions about enrollment, schedules, and services, and a website helper can answer common ones at any hour. The helper solves the problem of limited office hours and hard to find information by giving families a first place to ask. It must draw only on verified district information and state clearly when it does not know, so it does not mislead. Families should always be able to reach a person. A family resource directory can help families find services such as food assistance, health care, and tutoring, and a chat tool limited to a verified list can help them search it.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: The text does not give grade bands for this idea, so the practice is described for district and family settings rather than by grade. A chat tool on a district website can answer common questions at any hour. It should draw only on verified district information and say clearly when it does not know. Families should always be able to reach a person, and a staffed phone line and email should remain available and easy to find. A family resource directory can help families find services such as food assistance, health care, and tutoring, and a chat tool limited to a verified list can help families search it, with every resource checked regularly because services change.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book's evidence here is the Los Angeles case described in Chapter 3, which it presents as a warning. In that case, the vendor for the district's chatbot collapsed, and the district was left without the service it had paid for. The book does not cite a study or figure for website helpers or resource directories. So this idea rests on that case and on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: A website helper should never be the only way families can get help. A staffed phone line and email should remain available and easy to find. The tool should draw only on verified district information and say clearly when it does not know. It should never invent a resource that is not on the list, and every resource on the list should be checked regularly because services change. Decisions about what counts as verified information, what goes on the resource list, and how staffed help is maintained stay with people.
